extraction.name: MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark
extraction.description: MTEB is a comprehensive benchmark for text embeddings spanning 8 embedding tasks (bitext mining, classification, clustering, pair classification, reranking, retrieval, STS, and summarization) covering 58 datasets and 112 languages. It provides open-source code and a public leaderboard for evaluating any text embedding model.
extraction.creator: Niklas Muennighoff, Nouamane Tazi, Loïc Magne, Nils Reimers (Hugging Face, cohere.ai)
extraction.citeAs: Muennighoff et al., MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark, arXiv:2210.07316, 2023
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Datasets were collected from a combination of existing public benchmarks (e.g., BEIR, SemEval STS datasets), public APIs (arXiv, bioRxiv/medRxiv), Reddit posts, StackExchange posts, and Kaggle competitions. Some datasets were custom-made for MTEB using these sources.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web API, Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data sources include: public APIs from arXiv and bioRxiv/medRxiv for clustering datasets; Reddit posts and StackExchange posts for clustering datasets; existing benchmarks such as BEIR, SemEval STS datasets (STS12-STS22), Tatoeba, BUCC, Amazon reviews, Banking77, Emotion, IMDB, MASSIVE, MTOP, and others.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For ArxivClustering, abstracts are concatenated to the title in the P2P setting. For arXiv, only the first category is used when multiple categories are given. Subsets of labels are selected and articles sampled to yield splits with varying amounts and sizes of clusters.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Cluster labels for arXiv, bioRxiv, and medRxiv datasets are generated using categories given to the papers by humans. For bitext mining datasets (BUCC, Tatoeba), annotated pairs correspond to translated sentence pairs. Other datasets reuse annotations from their original sources (e.g., SemEval STS scores, Amazon review stars, intent labels).
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: MTEB uses versioning at dataset and software level. The community is invited to contribute new datasets, tasks, or metrics via pull requests. Results are available in JSON format on the Hugging Face Hub.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: MTEB average scores are biased towards tasks with many datasets, notably retrieval, classification and clustering, due to task imbalance. Data contamination between MTEB datasets and model training datasets is not controlled for.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: 1. Very long documents are missing; longest datasets have a few hundred words. 2. Task imbalance: summarization has only one dataset. 3. Multilinguality: retrieval and clustering are English-only. 4. No code datasets. 5. Focused solely on natural language, no other modalities.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: MTEB is intended for benchmarking and evaluating text embedding models across diverse tasks including bitext mining, classification, clustering, pair classification, reranking, retrieval, semantic textual similarity, and summarization. It serves as a gateway to finding universal text embeddings applicable to a variety of tasks.

name.evidence: To solve this problem, we introduce the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB).

description.evidence: MTEB spans 8 embedding tasks covering a total of 58 datasets and 112 languages. Through the benchmarking of 33 models on MTEB, we establish the most comprehensive benchmark of text embeddings to date.

url.evidence: MTEB comes with open-source code and a public leaderboard at https://github.com/embeddings-benchmark/mteb

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: These datasets are custom-made for MTEB using the public APIs from arXiv and bioRxiv/medRxiv... MTEB incorporates SemEval datasets (STS11 - STS22) and BEIR alongside a variety of other datasets from various tasks.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: For S2S datasets, the input text is simply the title of the paper, while for P2P the input text is the concatenation of the title and the abstract... for arXiv multiple categories can be given to a single paper so we only use the first one... we select subsets of all labels and then sample articles from those labels.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: The cluster labels are generated using categories given to the papers by humans... The annotated pairs here corresponds to a pairs of translated sentences, i.e. a sentence and its translation in the other language.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: Through versioning at a dataset and software level, we aim to make it easy to reproduce results in MTEB... We welcome task, dataset or metric contributions to the MTEB codebase as well as additions to the leaderboard via our automatic submission format.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: Task imbalance Tasks in MTEB have a different amount of datasets with summarization consisting of only a single dataset. This means MTEB average scores, which are computed over all datasets, are biased towards tasks with many datasets, notably retrieval, classification and clustering... Our scale of experiments and that of model pre-training make controlling for data contamination challenging. Thus, we ignore overlap of MTEB datasets with model training datasets in MTEB scores.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Long document datasets MTEB covers multiple text lengths (S2S, P2P, S2P), but very long documents are still missing... Task imbalance Tasks in MTEB have a different amount of datasets with summarization consisting of only a single dataset... MTEB contains multilingual classification, STS and bitext mining datasets. However, retrieval and clustering are English-only... MTEB does not contain any code datasets... We have focused solely on natural language applications.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: MTEB aims to provide clarity on how models perform on a variety of embedding tasks and thus serves as the gateway to finding universal text embeddings applicable to a variety of tasks.
